archive.g: Requested SHA, branch head, tested SHA, pushed SHA, and synthetic merge SHA are distinct. Never relabel one as another without exact proof.
archive.n: Bind every validation conclusion to the exact head being claimed. Record the PR/head SHA, failing or blocked command/check, what was reproduced locally, and any log/tooling limitation. Use the canonical CI or Cloud Build lane when authorized, and never upgrade incomplete evidence into a pass.
archive.t: Exact-head CI evidence is required before merge conclusions

archive.g: Focused -> aggregate -> external validation. Do not launch duplicate/stale aggregate work for the same exact SHA, and never let focused success substitute for required aggregate validation.
archive.n: Run deterministic focused tests first. Dedupe exact-SHA validation proposals, skip stale proposals, and normally run aggregate validation once for the exact final head. Fall back to aggregate when focused mapping is ambiguous.
archive.t: Run focused tests before aggregate validation

archive.g: Never return the first plausible candidate before the full bounded candidate set has been inspected and classified.
archive.n: Collect all candidates first, preserve provenance and repository identity, then apply the canonical selection rules. Route duplicate-conflicting, malformed-plus-valid, unsupported, or ambiguous candidate sets to explicit fail-closed/manual-review states.
archive.t: Linked-issue parsing must prefer explicit authoritative references

archive.g: Characterize current behavior and protect failure, ambiguity, boundedness, and no-side-effect paths with deterministic fixtures before changing automation behavior.
archive.n: Define the adversarial matrix before implementation and make ambiguity, contradictions, malformed or oversized inputs, distinct-but-similar cases, and no-change outcomes first-class fixtures. Treat the happy path as only one case in the contract.
archive.t: Fixture coverage must protect ambiguity and edge cases

archive.g: One valid page is not a complete scan. Never promote partial or unknown pagination evidence to complete repository state.
archive.n: Bind completeness to the requested scope, pagination state, repository identity, and exact revision. Require positive terminal pagination proof; incomplete, unknown, moved, or partial retrieval must remain explicit and fail closed/manual review.
archive.t: Repository scanners must prove retrieval completeness for the state being audited

archive.g: Evidence-read failures should fail closed at the decision layer, not crash the collection pipeline when safe classification remains possible.
archive.n: Make non-authoritative evidence collection tolerant of bounded read failures and let the acceptance layer classify missing evidence explicitly.
archive.t: External evidence collection should degrade to manual review instead of crashing

archive.g: Per-issue readiness never proves batch compatibility; parallel execution requires a fresh deterministic conflict/isolation decision over the composed set.
archive.n: Before parallel execution, produce a bounded readiness/conflict plan covering owner agent, dependencies, likely files touched, governed surfaces, validation requirements, and merge order. Classify each issue as parallel-safe, sequential-only, blocked, or manual-review, and recheck conflicts as repository state changes.
archive.t: Batch automation must detect file and governed-surface conflicts before parallel execution

archive.g: Do not make a parser/helper API migration breaking by default; compatibility promises, existing callers, and identity-bearing serialization must be verified before old behavior is retired.
archive.n: Inventory current callers and identity-bearing behavior before changing a parser/helper contract. Prefer additive defaulted fields or a narrow compatibility adapter, preserve existing serialized/constructor behavior where promised, add explicit legacy-caller fixtures, migrate consumers deliberately, and remove compatibility only after current callers are proven migrated.
archive.t: Preserve existing callers during parser and API contract migrations

archive.g: Never normalize a repository-qualified issue reference into a local issue number alone; repository identity is part of the authority boundary.
archive.n: Preserve repository identity through parsing and decision-making. Support GitHub's real reference forms, but when a target names another repository and the downstream acceptance contract is local-repository scoped, retain the qualified target as evidence and route to manual review.
archive.t: Cross-repository issue references must preserve repository identity

archive.g: Missing != malformed != ambiguous. Preserve the evidence state and its reason codes through every parser/compatibility boundary.
archive.n: Return structured states that preserve absence, malformed, conflicting, unsupported, stale, incomplete, and manual-review evidence separately. Malformed evidence must never be normalized into ordinary absence.
archive.t: Parser results must distinguish missing evidence from ambiguous evidence

archive.g: Contextual examples, quotations, comments, and code are evidence text, not issue authority; lexical context must be resolved before link semantics.
archive.n: Mask non-authoritative lexical contexts before resolving closing semantics, then test those contexts explicitly alongside real body closing instructions. Keep masked references visible only as non-authoritative evidence when useful; never let examples outrank an actual supported closing instruction.
archive.t: Quoted and example issue references must not silently become authoritative targets

archive.g: Do not invent semantic authority for unsupported phrases, locations, or reference forms; parser convenience cannot widen the external system's authority contract.
archive.n: Recognize only vocabulary and locations proven authoritative by the owning external contract. Preserve unsupported or conflicting authoritative-looking text as evidence, but route ambiguity to manual review instead of extending semantics heuristically.
archive.t: Unsupported authoritative phrases must route to manual review instead of heuristic guessing

archive.g: Do not remove or thin authoritative coding guidance merely because retrieval exists or appears cheaper; require a measured no-regression retrieval-quality gate first.
archive.n: Treat context thinning as an evidence-gated optimization. Benchmark the current authoritative baseline against retrieval-assisted variants using correctness/validation outcomes, retrieval precision and sufficiency, stale/conflict handling, hallucination or unsupported-guidance rate, and context/compute cost. Reduce default authoritative context only after a measured no-regression result and preserve a fail-closed fallback to GitHub authority.
archive.t: Do not thin authoritative coding documentation until retrieval quality is proven

archive.g: Do not spend implementation or CI compute proving a refactor whose reduction-to-risk ratio has not passed a bounded static value gate.
archive.n: Run a static value gate before implementation: prove at least several identical callers, quantify net reduction after helper overhead, preserve lifecycle semantics, and treat a no-change disposition as successful when value is too low.
archive.t: Prove a refactor is worth doing before paying for implementation and CI

archive.g: Never attribute a red pre-change baseline to the planned implementation or spend feature-work compute while baseline ownership remains unresolved.
archive.n: Run and record the immutable baseline first. If it is red, stop feature/refactor work and classify the failure as an existing defect, focused new defect, or transient infrastructure problem before changing code.
archive.t: A red immutable baseline is its own blocker; classify it before feature work

archive.g: Compatibility may preserve evidence it cannot interpret; it must never convert unknown evidence into absence.
archive.n: Round-trip unknown fields and provenance even when a consumer cannot act on them. Consumers may reject or route to manual review, but must not silently erase evidence.
archive.t: Preserve unknown fields and provenance through compatibility layers

archive.g: Never coerce an unsupported major version into a supported contract merely because fields look similar.
archive.n: Accept only explicitly supported compatibility ranges. Preserve unknown optional evidence when allowed, but route unsupported major versions and ambiguous aliases to manual review or a fail-closed result.
archive.t: Unsupported major contract versions should fail closed, not be coerced

archive.g: Advisory only. GitHub code, tests, standards, issue contracts, authorization, and validation always outrank this record. Exact support is only hypothesis==6.165.9; no broader range or permanent dependency adoption is established.
archive.n: Retrieve this advisory lesson only when a Python task materially needs property/invariant generation, strategy design, shrinking, malformed-input exploration, or Hypothesis-specific debugging. Prefer ordinary pytest for exact closed vocabularies, known deterministic regressions, package/version assertions, or when current code/tests already answer the question.
archive.t: Use Hypothesis selectively for property-based testing and debugging

archive.g: After a governed coding or PR repair attempt remains red, do not begin another repair hypothesis or repository mutation until CKR6 material-use evaluation has been rerun, applicable Lessons Learned have been consumed or explicitly classified not-material/unavailable, and the failed hypothesis is preserved in the diagnostic state.
archive.n: Every failed implementation or repair attempt is a mandatory re-entry trigger: preserve the failed hypothesis and durable checkpoint, record any side defect, rerun CKR6 material-use planning, consume only bounded relevant Lessons Learned, record consumed/not-material/unavailable, reacquire GitHub truth, then form the next hypothesis. Continue the branch/PR lineage unless proven unusable. GitHub code, tests, governance, and exact-head evidence are authoritative; Notion Lessons Learned remain advisory.
archive.t: Failed repair attempts must re-enter CKR6 Lessons Learned preflight before another repair hypothesis

archive.g: Exhaust bounded owner-correct diagnostic alternatives before declaring a blocker or assigning evidence retrieval to the repository owner.
archive.n: When one diagnostic surface is insufficient, continue through bounded authorized alternatives in the same lineage. Only declare a blocker after those alternatives are exhausted, with the actual missing capability and clearing owner named.
archive.t: Surface failure is not mission failure

archive.g: Do not stop at red status, run identity, failed-job identity, or failing-step name when actionable failure evidence is still retrievable.
archive.n: Treat status/run/job metadata as diagnostic progress only. Continue until the first actionable failure is obtained or a finite diagnostic-evidence-unavailable result is proven after bounded reroute.
archive.t: Red CI status is intermediate evidence, not diagnosis

archive.g: A failing repository-wide check must remain visible as failure, but it is not automatically proof that the current PR introduced the defect.
archive.n: Classify aggregate failure provenance before PR attribution. Record the exact PR head SHA, failing check/job/package, whether it reproduces on the PR head and on plain current main, and any log/tooling limitation. If PR-specific validation is green but an unrelated required aggregate failure remains, report the status precisely as: “PR-specific checks green; blocked by an unrelated aggregate-validation failure,” track that defect separately, do not patch it into the PR, and respect the rerun budget.
archive.t: Aggregate-red requires provenance before PR attribution

archive.g: Logging a side defect is progress, not completion. Hand control back to the original authorized mission; do not treat the side-defect record as the mission's end.
archive.n: After recording or hardening a non-blocking Agent OS defect, immediately hand control back to the original authorized mission in the same lineage. Do not require another continue, finish, complete-handoff, or work-on prompt. A side-defect write is subordinate evidence, not parent completion. Stop only for a genuine shared authorization, source-of-truth, scope, excluded-surface, material-decision, external-system, safety, or no-capable-route blocker.
archive.t: Recording a side defect is not completion of the original mission

archive.g: Capability discovery is intermediate evidence, not task completion. After a successful discovery, immediately perform the next admitted action in the same lineage.
archive.n: After discovering a usable capability, immediately continue to the next admitted operation in the same lineage. If that capability is insufficient, consume the existing reroute semantics; if no capable authorized route exists, return an explicit blocker. Discovery alone never satisfies the mission.
archive.t: Successful capability discovery is not successful task execution

archive.g: Validation must be head-aware and evidence-aware. Never duplicate an in-flight or completed check for the same head without a specific reason documented in the run.
archive.n: Before launching or rerunning validation, compare the exact current head SHA, changed scope, and all existing check/build evidence. Reuse valid exact-head results; do not manually trigger aggregate validation when an equivalent run for that head is already queued, running, or complete. Run focused tests first and invalidate only evidence affected by a code change.
archive.t: Do not rerun validation that is already valid for the current head

archive.g: Fail safe on linked-issue ambiguity. Preserve repository identity for qualified references; never reduce ambiguous or cross-repository evidence to an unqualified local issue number.
archive.n: Automatically resolve a linked issue only when exactly one unique target is identified by a documented explicit GitHub closing keyword: close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed, or resolve/resolves/resolved. Bare #issue references are non-authoritative. Multiple or conflicting explicit targets, unsupported authoritative phrases, or unresolved repository identity must route to manual review rather than selecting the first match.
archive.t: Linked-issue parsing must fail safe

archive.g: PR scope follows its diff and linked issue, not every red aggregate check.
archive.n: Never patch unrelated CI failures into the PR. Record the exact-head SHA, failing check/package, local reproduction result, and tooling or log-access limitations. Respect rerun budgets. If PR-specific checks are green while unrelated aggregate validation is red, state that precisely and continue all remaining in-scope validation.
archive.t: Separate PR-specific failures from unrelated aggregate CI failures

archive.g: A contract test is repository truth. Change it only when the governed artifact intentionally changed; never delete, relax, or skip it merely to turn a check green.
archive.n: When a PR modifies a governed/versioned artifact, identify repository contract tests pinning that artifact's version, structure, required literals, or size constraints. When aggregate validation fails, reproduce the failing contract against the PR diff and compare with a clean-main control before blaming CI infrastructure. Do not weaken a valid contract merely to make CI green: update the contract when an intentional governed change changes it, or repair the PR when the PR violated the existing contract.
archive.t: Governed-artifact changes must reconcile the contract tests that pin them

archive.g: No stale-head validation and no duplicate validation without a reason. Exact-head evidence is authoritative only for the head it actually tested.
archive.n: Bind validation evidence to the exact commit SHA. Before rerunning anything, inventory existing checks and evidence for the current head. Reuse still-valid exact-head results. If the head changed, rerun the affected focused tests and required aggregate/authoritative validation. Never claim a command ran when the execution environment could not run it; use the governed external validation lane when required.
archive.t: Validation evidence is head-specific; reuse valid exact-head evidence and rerun only what changed or is missing

archive.g: Prefer an obvious manual-review result over a polished acceptance report evaluated against the wrong issue.
archive.n: Automatically resolve a linked issue only when exactly one unique target is introduced by a documented explicit GitHub closing keyword: close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed, or resolve/resolves/resolved. Bare #issue references are non-authoritative. Multiple or conflicting explicit targets, unsupported authoritative phrases, malformed authority, or unresolved repository identity must route to manual review. Preserve repository identity for qualified references.
archive.t: Linked-issue resolution must fail safe and preserve repository identity

archive.g: GitHub mergeable=false is evidence to investigate, not sufficient proof of a semantic conflict.
archive.n: For refresh/reconciliation, let the deterministic reconciliation or git merge-tree path determine whether the branch can be refreshed. Only a genuine merge conflict should fail closed. When a genuine conflict is detected, do not push speculative changes.
archive.t: PR refresh must test deterministic reconciliation before treating mergeable=false as a conflict

archive.g: Do not declare continuation repaired solely because repository code emits agent_os_continuation or because a subordinate mutation succeeded. Require a native-host canary proving the parent mission continues without an unnecessary user prompt.
archive.n: When validating mission continuation, test the host boundary end-to-end. Treat subordinate writes as progress, not parent completion. Require the execution host to consume continuation state and automatically resume bounded authorized work until a governed terminal state, a real blocker, or an authorization boundary is reached.
archive.t: Native execution hosts must enforce continuation; emitted continuation metadata alone is insufficient

archive.g: Surface failure is not mission failure. Never claim a required check passed when it did not run; obtain equivalent exact-head evidence through an authorized reachable validation surface.
archive.n: Preserve the exact target SHA, record why the local surface is unavailable, and move the required check to an authoritative reachable validation lane. Do not substitute stale evidence, and do not stop merely because one validation surface failed.
archive.t: Validation evidence must be exact-head and environment-reachable; blocked local validation is not a reason to stop the mission

archive.g: legacy behavior -> canonical owner -> live consumer -> regression evidence -> current-main recheck -> deletion -> readback/absence proof
archive.n: Before retiring code, require: legacy behavior -> canonical owner -> live consumer -> regression evidence -> current-main recheck -> deletion -> readback/absence proof. Treat 'zero production consumers' as investigation evidence, not deletion authority. Make invariant mapping, production-consumer verification, test disposition, and current-main reconciliation explicit retirement prerequisites from the start. Serialize multi-file GitHub mutations that advance the same branch head.
archive.t: Retire architectures, not invariants.

archive.g: A red check right after someone else's merge is a moved-main suspect until reproduced on current main.
archive.n: On a check failure, check whether main advanced since the branch refresh; reproduce on current main before diagnosing the PR. Refresh to current main, re-run, and enforce the merge with the exact validated head.
archive.t: When a check fails right after another PR merges to main, reproduce on current main before diagnosing the PR.

pagination.n: Reject duplicate GitHub issue comment IDs across all pages.

pagination.g: Keep duplicate GitHub issue comment IDs across pages.
pagination.n: Reject duplicate GitHub issue comment IDs across all pages.

pagination_opposite.g: Keep duplicate GitHub issue comment IDs across pages.
pagination_opposite.n: Reject duplicate GitHub issue comment IDs across all pages.

receipts.n: Reject oversized GitHub HTTP GET response bytes and verify timestamp provenance.
receipts.t: GitHub HTTP GET response size and timestamp provenance

receipts.g: Accept oversized GitHub HTTP GET response bytes.
receipts.n: Reject oversized GitHub HTTP GET response bytes and verify timestamp provenance.
receipts.t: GitHub HTTP GET response size and timestamp provenance

receipts_opposite.g: Accept oversized GitHub HTTP GET response bytes.
receipts_opposite.n: Reject oversized GitHub HTTP GET response bytes and verify timestamp provenance.
receipts_opposite.t: GitHub HTTP GET response size and timestamp provenance

writer.n: After a Notion write, use an independent readback to verify the persisted revision.

writer_before.n: Before a Notion write, use an independent readback to verify the persisted revision.

writer_reversed.n: Use an independent readback to verify the persisted revision, then perform the Notion write.
